title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第三十六 孝義 Volume 55 Biographies 36: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第五十五‧列傳第三十六 孝義

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biography 36: Filial Piety and Righteousness
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biography 36: Filial Piety and Righteousness

sentences.zh: 崔懷慎 公孫僧遠 吳欣之 韓係伯 孫淡 華寶 韓靈敏 封延伯 吳達之 王文殊 朱謙之 蕭叡明 樂頤 江泌 杜栖 陸絳

translations.literal: Cui Huaishen, Gongsun Sengyuan, Wu Xinzhi, Han Xibo, Sun Dan, Hua Bao, Han Lingmin, Feng Yanbo, Wu Dazhi, Wang Wenshu, Zhu Qianzhi, Xiao Ruiming, Le Yi, Jiang Bi, Du Qi, Lu Jiang
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huaishen, Gongsun Sengyuan, Wu Xinzhi, Han Xibo, Sun Dan, Hua Bao, Han Lingmin, Feng Yanbo, Wu Dazhi, Wang Wenshu, Zhu Qianzhi, Xiao Ruiming, Le Yi, Jiang Bi, Du Qi, and Lu Jiang

sentences.zh: 子曰：「父子之道，天性也，君臣之義也。

translations.literal: The Master said: "The way of father and son is of nature; it is also the principle of ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The bond between father and son is innate; it is also the bond that defines ruler and minister."

sentences.zh: 」人之含孝稟義，天生所同，淳薄因心，非俟學至。

translations.literal: When people embody filial piety and bear righteous principle, it is innate to all from birth; purity or coarseness follow the heart, not awaiting learning to attain.
translations.idiomatic: To carry filial feeling and righteous duty is something all share from birth; whether one is pure or coarse follows the heart, not something that must be learned to arrive at.

sentences.zh: 遲遇為用，不謝始庶之法，驕慢之性，多慚水菽之享。

translations.literal: When treated with delay one still serves; one does not decline the rites owed an uncle born of a concubine. Those of arrogant nature are often ashamed at the meager offering of water and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Even when treated coldly one still serves; one does not refuse the mourning rites owed a humble-born uncle. An arrogant temperament, by contrast, is often ashamed of the plain fare of water and beans.

sentences.zh: 夫色養盡力，行義致身，甘心壟畝，不求聞達，斯即孟氏三樂之辭，仲由負米之歎也。

translations.literal: To nourish parents in countenance with utmost effort, to enact righteousness with one's person, to be content in the fields and not seek renown—this is the sense of Mencius's three pleasures and of Zhong You's lament over carrying rice on his back.
translations.idiomatic: To delight one's parents in every look, to give one's body to righteous action, to be content tilling the soil and never seek fame—this is what Mencius called the three joys, and what Zhong You meant when he sighed over carrying rice on his back.

sentences.zh: 通乎神明，理緣感召。

translations.literal: When it penetrates to the divine, principle arises through sympathetic response.
translations.idiomatic: When feeling reaches the spirits, principle answers through sympathetic response.

sentences.zh: 情澆世薄，方表孝慈。

translations.literal: In an age when sentiment runs thin and the world is shallow, filial kindness and compassion must be displayed outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Only when feeling has run thin and the age grown shallow must filial love and kindness be shown for all to see.

sentences.zh: 故非內德者所以寄心，懷仁者所以標物矣。

translations.literal: Hence those without inner virtue must lodge their hearts elsewhere, and those who cherish benevolence must mark themselves by deed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why those lacking inner virtue must set their hearts on outward things, and those who cherish benevolence must prove it in what they do.

sentences.zh: 埋名韞節，鮮或昭著，紀夫事行，以列于篇。

translations.literal: They bury their names and wrap their integrity, and few become manifest; here we record their conduct and set them forth in these pages.
translations.idiomatic: They hide their names and wrap away their integrity, and few ever come to light; here their deeds are recorded and set down in these pages.

sentences.zh: 崔懷慎，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Huaishen was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huaishen was from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父邪利，魯郡太守，宋元嘉中，沒虜。

translations.literal: His father Xieli was Administrator of Lu Commandery; in the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of Song he was captured by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xieli had been Administrator of Lu Commandery; during the Yuanjia reign of Emperor Wen of Song he was taken captive by the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 懷慎與妻房氏篤愛，聞父陷沒，即日遣妻，布衣蔬食，如居喪禮。

translations.literal: Huaishen was deeply devoted to his wife, née Fang. Upon hearing that his father had fallen captive, that very day he dismissed his wife, wore cloth garments and ate plain food, as though observing mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen loved his wife, née Fang, deeply. When he heard his father had been captured, that same day he sent his wife away, wore rough cloth, ate plain food, and lived as though in mourning.

sentences.zh: 邪利後仕虜中書，戒懷慎不許如此，懷慎得書更號泣。

translations.literal: Later Xieli served among the barbarians as Director of the Secretariat and admonished Huaishen not to behave thus; when Huaishen received the letter he wept afresh.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli later served the northern court as Director of the Secretariat and warned Huaishen not to act this way; when Huaishen received the letter he wept all the harder.

sentences.zh: 懷慎從叔模為滎陽太守，亦同沈虜，模子雖居處改節，而不廢婚宦。

translations.literal: Huaishen's uncle Mo was Administrator of Xingyang and likewise sank into captivity among the barbarians; Mo's sons, though they altered their conduct in residence, did not cease marrying and taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen's uncle Mo had been Administrator of Xingyang and likewise fell captive to the north; Mo's sons changed their way of life in exile, yet still married and took office.

sentences.zh: 大明中，懷慎宗人冀州刺史元孫北使，虜問之曰：「崔邪利、模竝力屈歸命，二家子姪，出處不同，義將安在？

translations.literal: In the Daming era, Huaishen's clansman Yuan Sun, Governor of Jizhou, went north on a mission; the barbarians questioned him, saying, "Cui Xieli and Mo both exhausted their strength and submitted to our command. Their respective nephews conduct themselves differently—where does righteousness lie?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era Huaishen's kinsman Yuan Sun, Governor of Jizhou, went north on embassy. The northerners asked him, "Cui Xieli and Mo both bowed to force and submitted. Yet their nephews behave so differently—where does righteousness stand?"

sentences.zh: 」元孫曰：「王尊驅驥，王陽回車，欲令忠孝竝弘，臣子兩節。」

translations.literal: Yuan Sun said, "Wang Zun drove out the fine steed while Wang Yang turned the carriage back—they wished to let loyalty and filial piety be displayed together, so that subject and son might observe both norms."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Sun replied, "Wang Zun drove the fine steed onward while Wang Yang turned the carriage back—they meant to let loyalty and filial piety shine together, so that subject and son might each keep their proper measure."

sentences.zh: 泰始初，淮北陷沒，界上流奔者，多有去就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era, when the north bank of the Huai fell, many refugees on the border fled one way or another.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taishi era the north bank of the Huai was lost, and many who fled across the border wavered between staying and leaving.

sentences.zh: 懷慎因此入北。

translations.literal: Huaishen accordingly went north.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen went north for that reason.

sentences.zh: 至桑乾，邪利時已卒，懷慎絕而後蘇。

translations.literal: When he reached Sanggan, Xieli had already died; Huaishen lost consciousness and only then revived.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanggan he learned Xieli had already died; Huaishen fainted and only then came to.

sentences.zh: 載喪還青州，徒跣冰雪，土氣寒酷，而手足不傷，時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: He bore the coffin back to Qing Province, going barefoot through ice and snow; the soil and climate were bitterly cold, yet his hands and feet were unharmed—people of the time took it as a response to filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the coffin back to Qing Province, walking barefoot through ice and snow in a land bitterly cold—yet his hands and feet were unharmed, and people called it a response to filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 喪畢，以弟在南，建元初，又逃歸，而弟亦已亡。

translations.literal: After the mourning was complete, because his younger brother was in the south, at the beginning of the Jianyuan era he fled back again, but his brother had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, knowing his younger brother was in the south, he fled back at the start of Jianyuan—only to find his brother had already died.

sentences.zh: 懷慎孤貧獨立，宗黨哀之，日斂給其升米。

translations.literal: Huaishen lived alone in destitution; his clan and kin pitied him and each day collected and gave him a measure of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen lived alone in poverty; his clan pitied him and each day pooled a measure of rice for him.

sentences.zh: 永明中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yongming era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yongming reign.

sentences.zh: 公孫僧遠，會稽剡人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Sengyuan was a man of Shan in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Sengyuan was from Shan in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 治父喪至孝，事母及伯父甚謹，年饑穀貴，僧遠省餐減食，以供母、伯。

translations.literal: In mourning his father he was utterly filial; he served his mother and his father's elder brother with great care. When famine made grain dear, Sengyuan cut his own portions to supply his mother and uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father with utmost filial piety and served his mother and paternal uncle with scrupulous care. In years of famine, when grain was dear, Sengyuan ate less so his mother and uncle might eat.

sentences.zh: 弟亡，無以葬，身販貼與隣里，供斂送之費。

translations.literal: When his younger brother died he had no means for burial; he sold himself to neighbors to raise funds for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother died he had nothing for the burial; he sold himself to neighbors to pay for the laying-out and funeral.

sentences.zh: 躬負土，手種松柏。

translations.literal: He shouldered the earth himself and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the earth on his own back and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 兄姊未婚嫁，乃自賣為之成禮。

translations.literal: His elder sisters were not yet married; he sold himself again to provide their weddings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sisters were still unmarried, so he sold himself again to provide their weddings.

sentences.zh: 名聞郡縣。

translations.literal: His fame spread through the commandery and counties.
translations.idiomatic: His name spread through the commandery and counties.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遣兼散騎常侍虞炎等十二部使行天下，建元三年，表列僧遠等二十三人，詔竝表門閭，蠲租稅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, he sent twelve groups of envoys, including the Acting Regular Cavalier Attendant Yu Yan, to tour the realm; in the third year of Jianyuan they memorialized twenty-three persons including Sengyuan; an edict ordered that their gateposts be posted and taxes remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took the throne he sent twelve touring envoys, among them the Acting Regular Cavalier Attendant Yu Yan, to travel the realm. In the third year of Jianyuan they memorialized twenty-three exemplars including Sengyuan; an edict ordered their gates posted with honor rolls and their taxes remitted.

sentences.zh: 吳欣之，晉陵利城人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xinzhi was a man of Licheng in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xinzhi was from Licheng in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，弟尉之為武進縣戍，隨王誕起義，太初遣軍主華欽討之，吏民皆散，尉之獨留，見執將死。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era his younger brother Weizhi was garrisoned at Wujin and followed Prince Dan of Langye in raising troops; in the Taichu era the commander Huaxin was sent to suppress them—the officials and people all scattered, but Weizhi alone remained and was seized on the point of death.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia his younger brother Weizhi was stationed at Wujin and followed Prince Dan of Langye in rebellion. In Taichu the commander Huaxin was sent against them; officials and commoners alike fled, but Weizhi alone stayed and was seized to be executed.

sentences.zh: 欣之詣欽乞代弟命，辭淚哀切，兄弟皆見原。

translations.literal: Xinzhi went to Huaxin to beg that he take his brother's place; his words and tears were bitter and earnest, and both brothers were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi went to Huaxin and begged to die in his brother's stead; his words and tears were desperate and piercing, and both brothers were spared.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，有詔蠲表。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan there was an edict remitting taxes and posting their gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict remitted their taxes and posted their gate.

sentences.zh: 永明初，廣陵民章起之二息犯罪爭死，太守劉悛表以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, among the people of Guangling, Qi of the Zhang family had two sons who quarreled over which should die for their crime; the Administrator Liu Juan reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, a Guangling man named Zhang Qi had two sons who had committed a crime and each insisted on dying in the other's place; Administrator Liu Juan reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 韓係伯，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Han Xibo was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xibo was from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 事父母謹孝。

translations.literal: He served his parents with scrupulous filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents with scrupulous filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 襄陽土俗，隣居種桑樹於界上為誌，係伯以桑枝蔭妨他地，遷堺上開數尺，隣畔隨復侵之，係伯輙更改種。

translations.literal: By custom in Xiangyang, neighbors planted mulberry trees on the boundary as markers; Xibo's mulberry branches shaded the neighbor's land, so he shifted the border marker several feet—yet the neighbor's plot kept encroaching again, and Xibo repeatedly moved and replanted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangyang custom neighbors planted mulberries on the boundary as markers. Xibo's mulberry branches shaded the neighbor's land, so he moved the border marker back several feet—but the neighbor's plot kept creeping in again, and Xibo only moved and replanted once more.

sentences.zh: 久之，隣人慚愧，還所侵地，躬往謝之。

translations.literal: After a long while the neighbor felt ashamed, returned the seized land, and came in person to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: In time the neighbor was ashamed, returned the land he had taken, and came in person to apologize.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，蠲租稅，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan his taxes were remitted and his gate posted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan his taxes were remitted and his gate posted with honor.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: He died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 孫淡，太原人也。

translations.literal: Sun Dan was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dan was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 居長沙，事母孝，母疾，不眠食，以差為期。

translations.literal: He lived in Changsha and was filial to his mother; when she fell ill he neither slept nor ate, setting her recovery as his term.
translations.idiomatic: Living in Changsha, he was filial to his mother; when she fell ill he neither slept nor ate, and would not stop until she recovered.

sentences.zh: 母哀之，後有疾，不使知也。

translations.literal: His mother pitied him; afterward whenever she was ill she did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: His mother pitied him; after that, whenever she fell ill she kept it from him.

sentences.zh: 豫章王領湘州，辟驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, holding Xiangzhou, appointed him Retainer on the Staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, governing Xiangzhou, appointed him Retainer on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，蠲租稅，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan taxes were remitted and the gate posted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan his taxes were remitted and his gate posted.

sentences.zh: 卒于家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 華寶，晉陵無錫人也。

translations.literal: Hua Bao was a man of Wuxi in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Bao was from Wuxi in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 父豪，義熙末，戍長安，寶年八歲。

translations.literal: His father Hao, at the end of the Yixi era, was stationed at Chang'an; Bao was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao was posted to Chang'an at the end of Yixi; Bao was eight.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂寶曰：「須我還，當為汝上頭。

translations.literal: At parting his father said to Bao, "When I return I shall arrange your capping for you."
translations.idiomatic: As he left he told Bao, "When I come back I will cap you myself."

sentences.zh: 」長安陷虜，豪歿。

translations.literal: Chang'an fell to the barbarians and Hao perished.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an fell to the northern armies and Hao died.

sentences.zh: 寶年至七十，不婚冠，或問之者，輙號慟彌日，不忍答也。

translations.literal: When Bao reached seventy he neither married nor capped himself; if anyone asked him, he wailed for days and could not bear to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Bao lived to seventy without marrying or taking the cap; if anyone asked why, he would wail for days on end and could not bring himself to answer.

sentences.zh: 同郡薛天生，母遭艱菜食，天生亦菜食，母未免喪而死，天生終身不食魚肉。

translations.literal: In the same commandery, Xue Tiansheng—when his mother was in mourning ate only vegetables, and Tiansheng ate only vegetables too; before his mother had finished mourning she died, and Tiansheng never ate fish or flesh for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the same commandery, Xue Tiansheng ate only vegetables while his mother mourned, and he ate only vegetables as well; she died before her mourning term ended, and Tiansheng never touched fish or meat again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 與弟有恩義。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother were bound by loving duty.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother were bound by deep affection and duty.

sentences.zh: 又同郡劉懷胤與弟懷則，年十歲，遭父喪，不衣絮帛，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: Also in the same commandery, Liu Huaiyin and his younger brother Huai'ze, at age ten when their father died, wore no quilted silk and ate no salted vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Also in that commandery, Liu Huaiyin and his younger brother Huai'ze, when their father died at age ten, wore no padded silk and ate no salted food or vegetables with sauce.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，竝表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan their gateposts were posted together.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan their gates were posted together.

sentences.zh: 韓靈敏，會稽剡人也。

translations.literal: Han Lingmin was a man of Shan in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingmin was from Shan in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 早孤，與兄靈珍竝有孝性，尋母又亡，家貧無以營凶，兄弟共種衆半畝，朝採衆子，暮已復生，以此遂辦葬事。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he and his elder brother Lingzhen were both marked by filial feeling; soon after, their mother also died—the family was too poor to conduct the funeral, and the brothers jointly planted half a mu of amaranth; they picked the seeds in the morning and by evening it had grown again, and by this they were able to complete the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he and his elder brother Lingzhen were both deeply filial. Soon their mother died too; the family was too poor for a funeral, so the brothers planted half a mu of amaranth together—they gathered the seeds in the morning, and by evening the plants had grown again, and with that they were able to bury her.

sentences.zh: 靈珍亡，無子，妻卓氏守節不嫁，慮家人奪其志，未嘗告歸，靈敏事之如母。

translations.literal: Lingzhen died without sons; his wife, née Zhuo, kept her chastity and would not remarry, fearing the family would wrest her resolve—she never told them when she went home—and Lingmin served her as he would a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen died without sons. His wife, née Zhuo, kept her chastity and would not remarry, fearing the family would break her resolve; she never told them when she went to visit her own kin, and Lingmin served her as he would a mother.

sentences.zh: 晉陵吳康之妻趙氏，父亡弟幼，值歲饑，母老病篤，趙詣鄉里自賣，言辭哀苦，鄉里憐之，人人分升米相救，遂得免。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Wu Kangzhi of Jinling—her father had died and her younger brother was small; in a year of famine her aged mother fell gravely ill—Zhao went to the village to offer herself for sale, her words bleak with grief; the village pitied her and each person gave a measure of rice, and thus she escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of Wu Kangzhi of Jinling, had lost her father while her younger brother was still small. In a famine year her aged mother fell gravely ill; Zhao went to the village to sell herself, her pleas raw with grief. The villagers pitied her and each gave a measure of rice, and so the family was saved.

sentences.zh: 及嫁康之，少時夫亡，家欲更嫁，誓死不貳。

translations.literal: When she married Kangzhi, her husband soon died; the family wished to marry her again, but she swore she would not take a second husband.
translations.idiomatic: After she married Kangzhi her husband soon died; the family wanted to marry her again, but she swore she would die before taking a second husband.

sentences.zh: 義興蔣儁之妻黃氏，夫亡不重嫁，逼之，欲赴水自殺，乃止。

translations.literal: Also Huang, wife of Jiang Junzhi of Yixing—when her husband died she would not remarry; when pressed she tried to throw herself into the water to die, and they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, wife of Jiang Junzhi of Yixing, would not remarry after her husband died; when they pressed her she tried to drown herself, and they stopped.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，詔蠲租賦，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict remitted rent and taxes and posted their gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict remitted their rent and taxes and posted their gates.

sentences.zh: 又廣陵徐靈禮妻遭火救兒，與兒俱焚死。

translations.literal: Also the wife of Xu Lingli of Guangling, when fire broke out rescued her child and perished in the flames with him.
translations.idiomatic: Also the wife of Xu Lingli of Guangling, when fire broke out, ran to save her child and perished in the flames with him.

sentences.zh: 太守劉悛以聞。

translations.literal: The Administrator Liu Juan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Liu Juan reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 又會稽人陳氏，有三女，無男。

translations.literal: Also a Chen family of Kuaiji had three daughters and no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Also a Chen family of Kuaiji had three daughters and no sons.

sentences.zh: 祖父母年八九十，老耄無所知，父篤癃病，母不安其室。

translations.literal: Their grandparents were nearly ninety, senile and unaware; their father was gravely ill with paralysis, and their mother could not remain in the household peaceably.
translations.idiomatic: Their grandparents were nearly ninety, senile and helpless; their father was gravely ill and paralyzed; their mother could not keep peace in the household.

sentences.zh: 值歲飢，三女相率於西湖採菱蓴，更日至市貨賣，未嘗虧怠。

translations.literal: In a year of famine the three daughters together went to West Lake to gather water chestnuts and lotus stems, taking turns each day to sell them at market, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year the three daughters together gathered water chestnuts and lotus stems at West Lake, taking turns selling them in the market day after day without slackening.

sentences.zh: 鄉里稱為義門，多欲取為婦，長女自傷煢獨，誓不肯行。

translations.literal: The village called them a household of righteousness; many wished to take them as wives, but the eldest daughter, grieving her solitude, swore she would not go.
translations.idiomatic: The village called them a household of righteousness; many wished to marry them, but the eldest daughter, grieving her lonely duty, swore she would not leave.

sentences.zh: 祖父母尋相繼卒，三女自營殯葬，為菴舍墓側。

translations.literal: The grandparents soon died in succession; the three daughters arranged the burials themselves and built huts beside the graves.
translations.idiomatic: The grandparents soon died one after another; the three daughters arranged the burials themselves and built huts beside the tombs.

sentences.zh: 又永興概中里王氏女，年五歲，得毒病，兩目皆盲。

translations.literal: Also a Wang girl of Gaizhong village in Yongxing—at five years she contracted a poisonous illness and both eyes went blind.
translations.idiomatic: Also a Wang girl of Gaizhong village in Yongxing—at five she contracted a virulent illness and both eyes went blind.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，年二十，父母死，臨屍一呌，眼皆血出，小妹娥舐其血，左目即開，時人稱為孝感。

translations.literal: By nature supremely filial, at twenty when her parents died, at the corpses she gave one cry and blood poured from both eyes; her younger sister E licked the blood and the left eye opened—people of the time called it a response to filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was supremely filial. At twenty, when her parents died, she gave one cry over their bodies and blood poured from both eyes; her younger sister E licked the blood and her left eye opened—people called it a response to filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 縣令何曇秀不以聞。

translations.literal: The Magistrate He Yanxiu did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate He Yanxiu did not report it upstream.

sentences.zh: 又諸暨東洿里屠氏女，父失明，母痼疾，親戚相弃，鄉里不容。

translations.literal: Also a Tu family girl of Dong'ou village in Zhuji—her father lost his sight and her mother had a chronic illness; kin abandoned them and the village would not tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: Also a girl of the Tu family in Dong'ou village, Zhuji—her father was blind and her mother chronically ill; kin abandoned them and the village would not shelter them.

sentences.zh: 女移父母遠住苧羅，晝樵采，夜紡績，以供養。

translations.literal: The girl moved her parents far off to Zhiluo; by day she gathered firewood, by night she spun, to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The girl moved her parents far off to Mount Zhiluo; by day she gathered firewood, by night she spun, to support them.

sentences.zh: 父母俱卒，親營殯葬，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When both parents died she personally arranged the funeral and shouldered earth to mound the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When both parents died she arranged the funeral herself and carried earth to raise the mound.

sentences.zh: 忽聞空中有聲云：「汝至性可重，山神欲相驅使。

translations.literal: Suddenly a voice in the air said, "Your utmost sincerity is worthy of esteem; the mountain god wishes to send you forth as his agent."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a voice in the air said, "Your utmost sincerity is worthy of honor; the mountain god wishes to send you forth as his agent."

sentences.zh: 汝可為人治病，必得大富。

translations.literal: "If you heal people of their illness you will surely gain great wealth."
translations.idiomatic: "If you heal people's illnesses you will surely grow very rich."

sentences.zh: 」女謂是○魅，弗敢從，遂得病。

translations.literal: The girl took it for a demon and dared not obey; soon after she fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The girl took it for an evil spirit and dared not obey; soon after she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 積時，隣舍人有中溪蜮毒者，女試治之，自覺病便差，遂以巫道為人治疾，無不愈。

translations.literal: After some time a neighbor suffered the bite of a stream parasite; the girl tried to treat him and felt her own illness ease at once; thereafter she practiced shaman craft to heal others, and none went uncured.
translations.idiomatic: After some time a neighbor was stricken by a stream demon's poison; the girl tried to treat him and felt her own illness lift at once. Thereafter she practiced shaman healing for others, and none went uncured.

sentences.zh: 家產日益，鄉里多欲娶之，以無兄弟，誓守墳墓不肯嫁，為山賊劫殺。

translations.literal: Her household wealth grew day by day; many in the village wished to marry her, but having no brothers she swore to guard the graves and would not marry—later mountain bandits robbed and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Her household grew richer day by day; many in the village wished to marry her, but with no brothers she swore to guard the graves and would not wed—until mountain bandits robbed and killed her.

sentences.zh: 縣令于琳之具言郡，太守王敬則不以聞。

translations.literal: The Magistrate Yu Linzhi set it all forth to the commandery, but the Administrator Wang Jingze did not report it upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yu Linzhi reported the full matter to the commandery, but Administrator Wang Jingze did not pass it on to court.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，吳興乘公濟妻姚氏生二男，而公濟及兄公願、乾伯竝卒，各有一子欣之、天保，姚養育之，賣田宅為娶婦，自與二男寄止隣家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, Yao of the Yao clan, wife of Cheng Gongji of Wuxing, bore two sons; Gongji and his elder brothers Gongyuan and Ganbo all died, each leaving one son—Xinzhi and Tianbao—and Yao reared them, selling fields and houses to arrange their marriages, while she herself lodged with the two boys at a neighbor's.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwu, Yao, wife of Cheng Gongji of Wuxing, bore two sons—but Gongji and his elder brothers Gongyuan and Ganbo all died, each leaving one son, Xinzhi and Tianbao. Yao reared them, sold fields and houses to arrange their marriages, and lodged with the two boys at a neighbor's home.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔為其二子婚，表門閭，復徭役。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming decreed the marriages of her two sons, posted their gate, and remitted corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming decreed marriages for her two sons, posted their gate with honor, and remitted their corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 吳郡范法恂妻褚氏，亦勤苦執婦業。

translations.literal: Also Chu of the Chu clan, wife of Fan Faxun of Wu Commandery, likewise toiled bitterly and held fast to a wife's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chu, wife of Fan Faxun of Wu Commandery, likewise labored hard and held faithfully to a wife's duties.

sentences.zh: 宋昇明中，孫曇瓘謀反亡命，褚謂其子僧簡曰：「孫越州先姑之姉子，與汝父親則從母兄弟，交則義重古人。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era of Song, Sun Tanjuan rebelled and fled; Chu said to her son Sengjian, "Sun of Yuezhou is nephew to your father's elder aunt's sister by marriage—as kin he is your father's cousin by the maternal line, and in friendship their bond outweighs that of olden men."
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengming era of Song, Sun Tanjuan rebelled and fled. Chu told her son Sengjian, "Sun of Yuezhou is nephew to your father's elder aunt's sister—as kin he is your father's cousin on the maternal side, and in friendship their bond outweighs what men owed in olden days."

sentences.zh: 逃竄脫不免，汝宜收之。

translations.literal: "In flight he cannot escape capture—you ought to shelter him."
translations.idiomatic: "In flight he cannot escape forever—you should shelter him."

sentences.zh: 」曇瓘尋伏法，褚氏令僧簡往歛葬。

translations.literal: Tanjuan soon was executed by law; the Chu clan had Sengjian go to gather and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Tanjuan was soon executed; Chu had Sengjian go to gather his body and bury him.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，永明中卒。

translations.literal: Past seventy years, she died in the Yongming era.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, she died in the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 僧簡在都，聞病馳歸，未至而褚已卒，將殯，舉尸不起，尋而僧簡至焉。

translations.literal: Sengjian was in the capital; hearing of her illness he raced home but had not arrived before Chu died; when they were about to lay the body in the coffin they could not lift it—and soon Sengjian arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjian was in the capital; hearing she was ill he raced home, but had not arrived before Chu died. When they were about to lay her in the coffin they could not lift the body—until Sengjian arrived.

sentences.zh: 封延伯字仲璉，渤海人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yanbo, style name Zhonglian, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanbo, courtesy name Zhonglian, was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 有學行，不與世人交，事寡嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: He possessed learning and conduct and did not mingle with the world; he served his widowed sister-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He had learning and integrity, kept apart from worldly company, and served his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him Chief Clerk and recommended him as Cultivated Talent, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him Chief Clerk and recommended him as Cultivated Talent, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 後乃仕。

translations.literal: Only later did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he take office.

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖為豫州，啟太祖用為長史，帶梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Yuan Chongzu, as Governor of Yuzhou, reported to the Founding Emperor recommending him as Chief of Staff, concurrently Administrator of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chongzu was Governor of Yuzhou he memorialized the Founding Emperor to appoint Yanbo Chief of Staff, concurrently Administrator of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾自免，僑居東海，遂不至京師。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and resigned, lodging in Donghai, and henceforth never went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and resigned, settled in Donghai, and never again went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三世同財，為北州所宗附。

translations.literal: Three generations shared one estate; north of the river he was the man to whom clans attached.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations held property in common; in the northern regions clans looked to him as their anchor.

sentences.zh: 豫章王辟中兵，不就，卒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Central Army Officer, but he would not accept and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Central Army Officer; he declined and died.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，大使巡行天下，義興陳玄子四世一百七十口同居。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan the grand envoys toured the realm; in Yixing, Chen Xuanzi's four generations—one hundred seventy mouths—dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan the grand envoys toured the realm; in Yixing, Chen Xuanzi's household spanned four generations—one hundred seventy people living together.

sentences.zh: 武陵郡邵榮興、文獻叔八世同居。

translations.literal: In Wuling Commandery, Shao Rongxing and Wen Xianshu—eight generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuling Commandery, Shao Rongxing and Wen Xianshu kept eight generations under one roof.

sentences.zh: 東海徐生之、武陵范安祖、李聖伯、范道根五世同居。

translations.literal: In Donghai, Xu Shengzhi; in Wuling, Fan Anzu, Li Shengbo, and Fan Daogen—five generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shengzhi of Donghai, and Fan Anzu, Li Shengbo, and Fan Daogen of Wuling each had five generations living together.

sentences.zh: 零陵譚弘寶、衡陽何弘、華陽陽黑頭疏從四世同居，竝共衣食。

translations.literal: Tan Hongbao of Lingling, He Hong of Hengyang, and Yang Heitou of Huayang with his distant cousins—four generations dwelling together, all sharing food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hongbao of Lingling, He Hong of Hengyang, and Yang Heitou of Huayang with his more distant kinsmen lived four generations together, sharing food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 詔表門閭，蠲租稅。

translations.literal: An edict honored their gates and lanes and remitted rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued plaques for their gates and lanes and exempted them from rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 又蜀郡王續祖、華陽郝道福竝累世同爨。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Xuzu of Shu Commandery and Hao Daofu of Huayang both for successive generations shared one cooking hearth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuzu of Shu Commandery and Hao Daofu of Huayang likewise had many generations cooking from a single hearth.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，明帝詔表門閭，蠲調役。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, Emperor Ming issued an edict to honor their gates and lanes and remit corvée and labor levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwu, Emperor Ming ordered plaques for their gates and lanes and exempted them from corvée and labor service.

sentences.zh: 吳達之，義興人也。

translations.literal: Wu Dazhi was a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dazhi was from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 嫂亡無以葬，自賣為十夫客，以營冢槨。

translations.literal: When his sister-in-law died he had no means to bury her; he sold himself as a bondservant for ten households' corvée to provide grave and coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When his sister-in-law died he had nothing for her burial, so he sold himself into corvée service for ten households in order to pay for her grave and coffin.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟敬伯夫妻荒年被略賣江北，達之有田十畝，貨以贖之，與之同財共宅。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Jingbo and wife, in a famine year, were seized and sold north of the Yangzi; Dazhi had ten mu of fields, sold them to redeem them, and shared property and dwelling with them.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine his cousin Jingbo and Jingbo's wife were captured and sold north of the Yangzi. Dazhi had ten mu of land; he sold it to ransom them and then shared his property and home with them.

sentences.zh: 郡命為主簿，固以讓兄。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him Chief Clerk; he firmly yielded the post to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery appointed him Chief Clerk, but he steadfastly yielded the post to his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 又讓世業舊田與族弟，弟亦不受，田遂閑廢。

translations.literal: He also yielded the family's hereditary old fields to a clansman; the clansman too would not accept them, and the fields were left idle.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave the family's hereditary fields to a kinsman, but the kinsman would not take them either, and the land was left to lie fallow.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，詔表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, an edict honored his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan the court honored his household with a commemorative plaque.

sentences.zh: 河南辛普明僑居會稽，自少與兄共處一帳，兄亡，以帳施靈座，夏月多蚊，普明不以露寢見色。

translations.literal: Xin Puming of Henan sojourned in Kuaiji; from youth he and his brother shared one mosquito net. When his brother died he dedicated the net to the spirit seat. In summer mosquitoes were many; Puming did not show displeasure at sleeping in the open.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Puming of Henan lived as a migrant in Kuaiji. From boyhood he and his brother had shared one mosquito net; when his brother died he gave the net to the spirit seat. In summer the mosquitoes were thick, yet Puming never showed annoyance at sleeping without it.

sentences.zh: 兄將葬，隣人嘉其義，賻助甚多，普明初受，後皆反之。

translations.literal: When his brother was about to be buried, neighbors admired his righteousness and gave many funeral gifts; Puming at first accepted them, then returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: As his brother's burial approached, neighbors admired his devotion and sent many funeral gifts. Puming accepted them at first, then returned every one.

sentences.zh: 贈者甚怪，普明曰：「本以兄墓不周，故不逆來意。

translations.literal: The donors were greatly puzzled. Puming said, "At first I thought my brother's tomb was not complete, so I did not refuse your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The donors were astonished. Puming said, "I accepted at first because my brother's tomb was not yet complete, and I did not wish to turn away your kindness.

sentences.zh: 今何忍亡者餘物以為家財。

translations.literal: How now could I bear to make the dead man's leftover goods into family wealth?
translations.idiomatic: How could I now turn what belonged to the dead into household property?

sentences.zh: 」後遭母喪，幾至毀滅。

translations.literal: " Later he suffered his mother's death and nearly ruined himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when his mother died, his mourning nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史豫章王辟為議曹從事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, Governor of Yang Province, summoned him as Retainer of the Advisory Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, as Governor of Yang Province, appointed him Retainer in the Advisory Bureau.

sentences.zh: 年五十，卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 又有何伯璵，弟幼璵，俱厲節操。

translations.literal: There were also He Boxuan and his younger brother You Boxuan, both strict in integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: There were also He Boxuan and his younger brother You Boxuan, both men of stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 養孤兄子，及長為婚，推家業盡與之。

translations.literal: They reared their orphaned elder brother's son; when he grew up they married him and gave him the entire family estate.
translations.idiomatic: They raised their orphaned nephew, and when he came of age they married him off and turned over the whole family estate to him.

sentences.zh: 安貧枯槁，誨人不倦，鄉里呼為人師。

translations.literal: Content in poverty and gaunt in frame, they taught others without tiring; the village called them the people's teachers.
translations.idiomatic: They lived content in poverty, taught tirelessly, and their neighbors called them the village teachers.

sentences.zh: 郡守下車，莫不修謁。

translations.literal: Whenever a new prefect arrived, none failed to pay them a respectful visit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new prefect took office, every one of them came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，伯璵卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Boxuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Boxuan died.

sentences.zh: 幼璵少好佛法，翦落長齋，持行精苦。

translations.literal: You Boxuan from youth loved Buddhist teaching, shaved his head and kept long fasts, and pursued ascetic practice with stern rigor.
translations.idiomatic: You Boxuan had loved Buddhism since youth; he tonsured himself, kept long fasts, and lived an austere religious life.

sentences.zh: 梁初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 兄弟年竝八十餘。

translations.literal: The brothers were both over eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers lived past eighty.

sentences.zh: 王文殊，吳興故鄣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshu was a man of Gucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshu was from Gucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父沒虜，文殊思慕泣血，蔬食山谷三十餘年。

translations.literal: His father perished among the barbarians; Wenshu mourned with longing until he wept blood, eating vegetables in mountain valleys for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in the north. Wenshu mourned until he wept blood, and for more than thirty years he lived on vegetables in the hills and valleys.

sentences.zh: 太守謝板為功曹，不就。

translations.literal: Prefect Xie Ban appointed him Merit Officer; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xie Ban offered him the post of Merit Officer, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，太守孔琇之表曰：「文殊性挺五常，心符三教。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Prefect Kong Xiuzhi memorialized, saying, "Wenshu's nature upholds the Five Constants; his heart accords with the Three Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Prefect Kong Xiuzhi submitted a memorial saying, "Wenshu's character embodies the Five Constants and his heart is attuned to the Three Teachings.

sentences.zh: 以父沒獯庭，抱終身之痛，專席恒居，銜罔極之卹。

translations.literal: Because his father died in the Xiongnu court, he embraces lifelong pain, dwells always alone on a separate mat, and bears boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father died in the northern barbarian lands, he carries a grief meant to last his whole life, lives always apart on his own mat, and nurses a sorrow without limit.

sentences.zh: 服紵縞以經年，餌蔬菽以俟命，婚義滅於天情，官序空於素抱。

translations.literal: He wears coarse hemp and plain silk year after year, feeds on vegetables and beans while awaiting fate; marriage's obligations are extinguished in natural feeling, official rank is void in his plain resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he wears the coarsest mourning cloth and lives on vegetables and beans while waiting for death. Marriage has been swallowed by grief, and the career he once hoped for stands empty.

sentences.zh: 儻降甄異之恩，牓其閭里。

translations.literal: If he might receive the grace of special selection, let his lane be placarded in honor.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would grant him exceptional recognition, let his neighborhood be honored with a public plaque.

sentences.zh: 」鬱林詔牓門，改所居為「孝行里」。

translations.literal: " Emperor Deposed of Yulin ordered his gate placarded and changed his dwelling's place to "Lane of Filial Conduct."
translations.idiomatic: " The Deposed Emperor of Yulin ordered a plaque for his gate and renamed his neighborhood "Lane of Filial Conduct."

sentences.zh: 朱謙之字處光，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父昭之，以學解稱於鄉里。

translations.literal: His father Zhaozhi was famed in the village for learning and understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaozhi was known throughout the district for scholarship and insight.

sentences.zh: 謙之年數歲，所生母亡，昭之假葬田側，為族人朱幼方燎火所焚。

translations.literal: When Qianzhi was only a few years old his birth mother died; Zhaozhi had her provisionally buried beside the fields, and clansman Zhu Youfang's burning fire consumed the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhi was still a small child his birth mother died. Zhaozhi had her buried provisionally beside the fields, but a fire set by their kinsman Zhu Youfang burned the grave.

sentences.zh: 同產姉密語之，謙之雖小，便哀戚如持喪。

translations.literal: His full sister told him in secret; though Qianzhi was small, he grieved as though in mourning at once.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister told him in secret. Though he was only a child, he mourned as if he were keeping full funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 年長不婚娶。

translations.literal: When he grew older he would not marry.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he refused ever to marry.

sentences.zh: 永明中，手刃殺幼方，詣獄自繫。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he killed Youfang with his own hand and went to prison to bind himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era he slew Youfang with his own blade and then went to prison to surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 縣令申靈勗表上，別駕孔稚珪、兼記室劉璡、司徒左西掾張融牋與刺史豫章王曰：「禮開報仇之典，以申孝義之情；

translations.literal: Magistrate Shen Lingxu submitted a memorial upward; Vice-Prefect Kong Zhagui, Acting Recorder Liu Jin, and Left Western Clerk to the Minister of Works Zhang Rong sent a note to the Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, saying, "Rites open the statute of revenge to express the feeling of filial righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported the case to the throne. Vice-Prefect Kong Zhagui, Acting Recorder Liu Jin, and Western Clerk to the Minister of Works Zhang Rong wrote jointly to the Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the province: "The rites provide for vengeance so that filial duty may be fulfilled;

sentences.zh: 法斷相殺之條，以表權時之制。

translations.literal: law cuts off the article on mutual killing to display the regulation suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: the law forbids mutual killing to uphold the order required by the age.

sentences.zh: 謙之揮刃斬冤，旣申私禮；

translations.literal: Qianzhi swung his blade and cut down his enemy, already fulfilling private rite;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi drew his blade and struck down his enemy, thereby fulfilling private obligation;

sentences.zh: 繫頸就死，又明公法。

translations.literal: he bound his neck and went to die, again clarifying public law.
translations.idiomatic: he bound himself and submitted to death, thereby honoring public law as well.

sentences.zh: 今仍殺之，則成當世罪人；

translations.literal: If now he is still killed, he becomes this age's criminal;
translations.idiomatic: If he is executed now, he becomes a criminal of our own time;

sentences.zh: 宥而活之，即為盛朝孝子。

translations.literal: if pardoned and kept alive, he becomes this flourishing dynasty's filial son.
translations.idiomatic: if pardoned and allowed to live, he becomes a filial exemplar of this flourishing court.

sentences.zh: 殺一罪人，未足弘憲；

translations.literal: to kill one criminal is not enough to enlarge the statutes;
translations.idiomatic: To kill one offender does little to magnify the law;

sentences.zh: 活一孝子，實廣風德。

translations.literal: to keep alive one filial son truly broadens exemplary virtue.
translations.idiomatic: to spare one filial son truly spreads moral influence.

sentences.zh: 張緒陸澄，是其鄉舊，應具來由。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng are his village elders and should fully set forth how the matter arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng are elders of his home district and should be asked to report the full circumstances.

sentences.zh: 融等與謙之竝不相識，區區短見，深有恨然。

translations.literal: Rong and the others did not know Qianzhi at all; in our narrow short view we deeply regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and the others did not even know Qianzhi personally, and we deeply regret that our limited view may fall short.

sentences.zh: 」豫章王言之世祖，時吳郡太守王慈、太常張緒、尚書陸澄竝表論其事，世祖嘉其義，慮相復報，乃遣謙之隨曹虎西行。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Yuzhang spoke of it to the Founding Emperor; at that time Wu Commandery Prefect Wang Ci, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Cheng all memorialized on the affair. The Founding Emperor approved the righteousness but feared reciprocal revenge, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Yuzhang reported the matter to Emperor Wu. At the time Wu Commandery Prefect Wang Ci, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Cheng all submitted memorials on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's righteousness but feared a cycle of revenge, and so sent him west with Cao Hu's campaign.

sentences.zh: 將發，幼方子惲於津陽門伺殺謙之，謙之之兄選之又刺殺惲，有司以聞。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Youfang's son Yun lay in wait at Jinyang Gate and killed Qianzhi; Qianzhi's elder brother Xuanzhi in turn stabbed and killed Yun. The authorities reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Just before he set out, Youfang's son Yun ambushed and killed Qianzhi at Jinyang Gate. Qianzhi's elder brother Xuanzhi then stabbed Yun to death. The authorities reported both killings.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「此皆是義事，不可問。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "These are all righteous acts and must not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These were all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 」悉赦之。

translations.literal: " He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: " He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 吳興沈顗聞而歎曰：「弟死於孝，兄殉於義。

translations.literal: Shen Yan of Wuxing heard and sighed, saying, "The younger brother died in filial piety; the elder brother followed in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yan of Wuxing heard of it and sighed, "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 孝友之節，萃此一門。

translations.literal: The integrity of filial piety and brotherly love gathers in this one household.
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion and brotherly duty have met in a single family.

sentences.zh: 」選之字處林，有志節，著辯相論。

translations.literal: " Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, had resolve and integrity and wrote Discourse on Distinguishing Physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, was a man of purpose and integrity and wrote Discourse on Distinguishing Physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 幼時顧歡見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: In his youth Gu Huan saw him and marveled; he gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he so impressed Gu Huan that Gu gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 官至江夏王參軍。

translations.literal: He reached office as Staff Officer to the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Staff Officer to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 蕭叡明，南蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Ruiming was a man of Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ruiming was from Southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍諶從祖兄弟也。

translations.literal: He was a paternal cousin of Champion General Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was a cousin on his father's side of Champion General Xiao Chen.

sentences.zh: 父孝孫，左軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiaosun was Left Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaosun had been Left Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 叡明初仕員外殿中將軍。

translations.literal: Ruiming at first served as Supernumerary Palace Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Ruiming began his career as Supernumerary Palace Guard General.

sentences.zh: 少有至性，奉親謹篤。

translations.literal: From youth he had utmost nature, serving his parents with careful devotion.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply devoted and served his parents with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 母病躬禱，夕不假寐，及亡，不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person and at night did not close his eyes in sleep; when she died he could not bear his grief and perished.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person and slept not at all by night. When she died his grief overwhelmed him and he died.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，世祖詔曰：「龍驤將軍、安西中兵參軍、松滋令蕭叡明，愛敬淳深，色養盡禮，喪過乎哀，遂致毀滅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, the Founding Emperor's edict said, "Dragon-soaring General, Central Army Officer of the Anxi Command, and Magistrate of Songzi Xiao Ruiming—love and reverence pure and deep, supporting his parents in countenance with full rite, mourning beyond measure in grief, and thus brought to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming, Emperor Wu issued an edict: "Dragon-soaring General, Central Army Officer on the Anxi staff, and Magistrate of Songzi, Xiao Ruiming—his love and reverence were deep and sincere, his care for his parents fulfilled every ritual obligation, and his mourning exceeded all bounds until it destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 雖未達聖教，而一至可愍。

translations.literal: Though he did not reach the sage's teaching, his utmost sincerity is pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: He may not have attained the sage's standard, yet his single-minded devotion deserves pity.

sentences.zh: 宜加榮命，以矜善人。

translations.literal: He should receive added honored appointment to show regard for the good man.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted posthumous honors to commend the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 可贈中書郎。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously appointed Secretariat Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Secretariat Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 樂頤字文德，南陽涅陽人。

translations.literal: Le Yi, courtesy name Wende, was a man of Niyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yi, courtesy name Wende, was from Niyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 世居南郡。

translations.literal: His family for generations dwelt in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而言行和謹，仕為京府參軍。

translations.literal: From youth his words and conduct were harmonious and careful; he served as Staff Officer in the capital prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was gentle and careful in word and deed, and he served as a staff officer in the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父在郢州病亡，頤忽思父涕泣，因請假還，中路果得父凶問。

translations.literal: His father died of illness in Ying Province; Yi suddenly thought of his father and wept, therefore asked leave to return, and midway indeed received news of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill and died in Ying Province, Yi was suddenly overcome with longing and wept. He asked for leave to go home and on the road received confirmation of his father's death.

sentences.zh: 頤便徒跣號咷，出陶家後渚，遇商人附載西上，水漿不入口數日。

translations.literal: Yi went barefoot, wailing aloud, left by the rear ford at Tao's house, met a merchant and boarded westward; for several days he took no water or food.
translations.idiomatic: Yi went barefoot, wailing as he went, and left from the rear landing at Tao's place. He found a merchant's boat heading west and boarded it, and for days he would take neither food nor drink.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇病，與母隔壁，忍痛不言，齧被至碎，恐母之哀己也。

translations.literal: Once when he fell ill he lay separated from his mother only by a wall; he bore the pain without speaking and bit his quilt until it shredded, fearing his mother would grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he was ill he lay in the next room from his mother. He endured the pain in silence and chewed his quilt to shreds, lest she grieve over him.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史王僧虔引為主簿，以同僚非人，弃官去。

translations.literal: Wang Sengqian, Governor of Xiang Province, summoned him as Chief Clerk; because a colleague was unworthy, he abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian, Governor of Xiang Province, appointed him Chief Clerk, but when a colleague proved unworthy Yi resigned and left office.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎庾杲之嘗往候，頤為設食，枯魚菜菹而已。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Gentleman Yu Gaozhi once came to visit; Yi set out food for him—only dried fish and pickled vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gaozhi of the Ministry of Personnel once came to call on him. Yi served only dried fish and pickled vegetables.

sentences.zh: 杲之曰：「我不能食此。

translations.literal: Gaozhi said, "I cannot eat this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhi said, "I cannot eat this.

sentences.zh: 」母聞之，自出常膳魚羹數種。

translations.literal: " His mother heard and came out herself with several kinds of fish broth from the regular table.
translations.idiomatic: " When his mother heard, she came out herself with several kinds of fish soup from their usual fare.

sentences.zh: 杲之曰：「卿過於茅季偉，我非郭林宗。

translations.literal: Gaozhi said, "You go beyond Mao Jiwei; I am no Guo Linzong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhi said, "You are more extreme than Mao Jiwei, and I am no Guo Linzong.

sentences.zh: 」仕至郢州治中，卒。

translations.literal: " He served up to Administrative Advisor of Ying Province and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose to Administrative Advisor of Ying Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弟預亦孝，父臨亡，執其手以託郢州行事王奐，預悲感悶絕，吐血數升，遂發病。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu was also filial; as their father neared death he grasped Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, Acting Governor of Ying Province. Yu grieved until he fainted, spat blood by the sheng, and thereafter fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu was likewise filial. As their father lay dying he took Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, Acting Governor of Ying Province. Yu was so overcome with grief that he fainted, vomited several sheng of blood, and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 官至驃騎錄事。

translations.literal: He reached office as Recorder to the Rapid-as-Thunder General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Recorder on the staff of the Rapid-as-Thunder General.

sentences.zh: 隆昌末，預謂丹陽尹徐孝嗣曰：「外傳藉藉，似有伊周之事，君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷託付之重，恐不得同人此舉。

translations.literal: At the end of Longchang, Yu said to Xu Xiaosi, Governor of Danyang, "Outside rumor is noisy, as though there were an affair like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; you received Emperor Wu's extraordinary grace and bear the weight of his entrustment—I fear you cannot join others in this act.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Longchang reign, Yu said to Xu Xiaosi, Governor of Danyang, "Rumors are everywhere, as if something like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou were afoot. You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bear the burden of his trust. I fear you cannot go along with what others are plotting.

sentences.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。

translations.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu, and to this day teeth are cold with scorn.
translations.idiomatic: Men still mock Lord Chu, and the shame has not faded to this day.

sentences.zh: 」孝嗣心甚納之。

translations.literal: " Xiaosi inwardly greatly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaosi took the warning deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為永世令，民懷其德。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he served as Magistrate of Yongshi; the people cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era he served as Magistrate of Yongshi, and the people cherished his virtue.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 有一老嫗行擔斛蔌葉將詣市，聞預死，弃擔號泣。

translations.literal: An old woman was walking, carrying on a pole vegetable leaves to go to market; when she heard Yu had died she cast down her pole and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman was on her way to market with a pole-load of vegetable leaves. When she heard that Yu had died, she dropped her burden and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 鴈門解仲恭，亦僑居南郡。

translations.literal: Xie Zhonggong of Yanmen also sojourned in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhonggong of Yanmen likewise lived as a migrant in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 家行敦睦，得纖豪財利，輙與兄弟平分。

translations.literal: His household conduct was warm and harmonious; whenever he gained the slightest profit he at once divided it equally with his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His household was harmonious, and whenever he gained even the smallest profit he divided it equally among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 母病經時不差，入山採藥，遇一老父語之曰：「得丁公藤，病立愈。

translations.literal: His mother's illness for a long time did not improve; he entered the mountains to gather medicine and met an old man who told him, "Obtain Master Ding's vine and the illness will heal at once.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's illness lingered without improvement. He went into the mountains to gather herbs and met an old man who told him, "Find the Master Ding vine and the illness will be cured at once.

sentences.zh: 此藤近在前山際高樹垂下便是也。

translations.literal: This vine is near at hand on the front mountain slope, hanging down from a tall tree—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: It grows just ahead on the mountain slope, hanging from a tall tree—that is the one.

sentences.zh: 」忽然不見。

translations.literal: " Suddenly he was gone.
translations.idiomatic: " Then the old man vanished.

sentences.zh: 仲恭如其言得之，治病，母即差。

translations.literal: Zhonggong obtained it as he had said and treated the illness; his mother recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong found the vine as directed, prepared the medicine, and his mother recovered immediately.

sentences.zh: 至今江陵人猶有識此藤者。

translations.literal: To this day people of Jiangling still recognize this vine.
translations.idiomatic: Even now people in Jiangling still know this vine.

sentences.zh: 江泌字士清，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Bi, courtesy name Shiqing, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bi, courtesy name Shiqing, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 父亮之，員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Liangzhi was a Supernumerary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangzhi had been a Supernumerary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 泌少貧，晝日斫屟，夜讀書，隨月光握卷升屋。

translations.literal: Bi from youth was poor; by day he carved sandals, by night he read books, and following the moonlight he would grasp his scroll and climb onto the roof.
translations.idiomatic: Bi grew up in poverty. By day he carved sandals; by night he studied, and when moonlight fell on his pages he would take his scroll and climb onto the roof to read.

sentences.zh: 性行仁義，衣弊，恐虱饑死，乃復取置衣中。

translations.literal: In nature and conduct he was benevolent and righteous; when his clothes were worn, fearing lice might starve to death, he would take them back and place them in his garments.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and righteous. When his clothes were threadbare he feared the lice might starve, so he would gather them back into his garments.

sentences.zh: 數日閒，終身無復虱。

translations.literal: Within a few days, for the rest of his life he had no lice again.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the lice vanished, and he never had them again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 母亡後，以生闕供養，遇鮭不忍食。

translations.literal: After his mother died, because living things were lacking for her offerings, when he encountered salmon he could not bear to eat it.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he could not bear to use living creatures for her offerings; when he came upon salmon he could not bring himself to eat it.

sentences.zh: 食菜不食心，以其有生意也。

translations.literal: He ate vegetables but not their hearts, because they still held the spark of life.
translations.idiomatic: He ate vegetables but not their hearts, for they still held life within them.

sentences.zh: 歷仕南中郎行參軍，所給募吏去役，得時病，莫有舍之者，吏扶杖投泌，泌親自隱卹，吏死，泌為買棺。

translations.literal: He served as Retainer on the Staff of the Southern General of the Gentlemen of the Household; a conscript clerk assigned to him finished his term and fell ill with a seasonal disease—no one would take him in. The clerk leaned on his staff and came to Bi; Bi personally sheltered and comforted him. When the clerk died, Bi bought his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Retainer on the staff of the Southern General of the Gentlemen of the Household. A conscript clerk finishing his term fell ill with a seasonal sickness, and no one would shelter him; leaning on his staff the man came to Bi, who personally cared for him in secret. When the clerk died, Bi bought his coffin.

sentences.zh: 無僮役，兄弟共輿埋之。

translations.literal: He had no servants; he and his brothers together carried the coffin to burial.
translations.idiomatic: He had no servants; he and his brothers together bore the coffin to the grave.

sentences.zh: 領國子助教。

translations.literal: He held the post of Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 乘牽車至染烏頭，見老翁步行，下車載之，躬自步去。

translations.literal: Riding in a cart drawn by oxen to Ranyawutou, he saw an old man walking and got down to let him ride, while he himself walked away on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Riding in an ox-cart to Ranyawutou, he saw an old man walking, got down and gave him the cart, and walked on himself.

sentences.zh: 世祖以為南康王子琳侍讀。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor appointed him Reader to Prince Lin of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed him Reader to Prince Lin of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 建武中，明帝害諸王後，泌憂念子琳，詣誌公道人問其禍福。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era, after Emperor Ming harmed the princes, Bi worried over Zilin and went to the Daoist Master Zhigong to ask his fortune.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu, after Emperor Ming had killed the princes, Bi worried for Zilin and went to the Daoist Master Zhigong to ask what fate held for him.

sentences.zh: 誌公覆香鑪灰示之，曰：「都盡。

translations.literal: Zhigong overturned the incense burner and showed him the ashes, saying, "All is gone."
translations.idiomatic: Zhigong tipped over the incense burner and showed him the ashes, saying, "All is gone."

sentences.zh: 無所餘。

translations.literal: Nothing remains.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing remains.

sentences.zh: 」及子琳被害，泌往哭之，淚盡，繼之以血。

translations.literal: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him; his tears ran dry and were followed by blood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him; his tears ran dry and blood followed.

sentences.zh: 親視殯葬，乃去。

translations.literal: He personally oversaw the laying-out and burial, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He personally oversaw the funeral and burial, then left.

sentences.zh: 時廣漢王侍讀嚴桓之亦哭王盡哀。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Huanzhi, Reader to the Prince of Guanghan, likewise mourned the prince to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yan Huanzhi, Reader to the Prince of Guanghan, likewise mourned the prince with utmost grief.

sentences.zh: 泌尋卒。

translations.literal: Bi soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Bi soon died.

sentences.zh: 泌族人兖州治中泌，黃門郎悆子也，與泌同名。

translations.literal: A clansman of Bi named Bi, Administrator of Yanzhou, was son of the Yellow Gate Attendant Yu and bore the same name as Bi.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of Bi, also named Bi, was Administrator of Yanzhou and son of the Yellow Gate Attendant Yu; he bore the same given name.

sentences.zh: 世謂泌為「孝江泌」以別之。

translations.literal: The world called Bi "Filial Jiang Bi" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: People called him "Filial Jiang Bi" to distinguish him from the other.

sentences.zh: 杜栖字孟山，吳郡錢唐人，徵士京產子也。

translations.literal: Du Qi, style name Mengshan, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery, son of the recluse Jingchan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi, courtesy name Mengshan, was from Qiantang in Wu Commandery, son of the recluse Jingchan.

sentences.zh: 同郡張融與京產相友，每相造言論，栖常在側。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was friends with Jingchan; whenever they visited each other to discuss learning, Qi was always at their side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was friends with Jingchan; whenever they visited each other to talk, Qi was always at their side.

sentences.zh: 融指栖曰：「昔陳太丘之召元方，方之為劣。

translations.literal: Rong pointed to Qi and said, "In olden days when Chen Taqiu summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was judged inferior."
translations.idiomatic: Rong pointed to Qi and said, "When Chen Taqiu once summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was judged the lesser man."

sentences.zh: 以今方古，古人何貴。

translations.literal: Comparing the present with antiquity, why should the ancients be prized?
translations.idiomatic: Set the present beside antiquity, and what is there to prize in the ancients?

sentences.zh: 」栖出京師，從儒士劉瓛受學。

translations.literal: Qi left the capital and studied under the scholar Liu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi left the capital and studied under the scholar Liu Huan.

sentences.zh: 善清言，能彈琴飲酒，名儒貴遊多敬待之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in pure conversation, could play the zither and drink wine, and eminent scholars and noble travelers all treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at pure talk, played the zither and drank well, and eminent scholars and noble travelers alike treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 中書郎周顒與京產書曰：「賢子學業清標，後來之秀。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Lang Zhou Yong wrote to Jingchan, saying, "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a talent of the rising generation."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong, Secretariat Gentleman, wrote to Jingchan, "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a talent of the rising generation."

sentences.zh: 嗟愛之懷，豈知云已。

translations.literal: My sighing affection for him—how can I say it has ended?
translations.idiomatic: My affection for him runs so deep I cannot say it has ended.

sentences.zh: 所謂人之英彥，若己有之也。

translations.literal: What is called a splendid man among people—I cherish him as if he were my own.
translations.idiomatic: He is the sort of splendid man one cherishes as though he were one's own.

sentences.zh: 」刺史豫章王聞其名，辟議曹從事，仍轉西曹佐。

translations.literal: The Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, heard his name and appointed him Retainer in the Bureau of Deliberation, then transferred him to Western Bureau Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, as Governor, heard his name and appointed him Retainer in the Bureau of Deliberation, then made him Assistant in the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良數致禮接。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling repeatedly sent him courteous invitations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling repeatedly honored him with invitations.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒何胤治禮，又重栖，以為學士，掌婚冠儀。

translations.literal: He Yin, Director of the Imperial University, was versed in ritual and also valued Qi, making him Academician in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin, Director of the Imperial University, was versed in ritual and also esteemed Qi, appointing him Academician in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以父老歸養，怡情壟畝。

translations.literal: Because his father was aged he returned home to support him, finding contentment in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When his father grew old he went home to support him, finding peace in the fields.

sentences.zh: 栖肥白長壯，及京產疾，旬日閒便皮骨自支。

translations.literal: Qi was plump, fair, tall, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days he was reduced to skin and bone himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had been plump, fair-skinned, tall, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days he was skin and bone himself.

sentences.zh: 京產亡，水漿不入口七日，晨夕不罷哭，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: When Jingchan died, Qi took no food or drink for seven days, wept morning and evening without cease, and ate no salted vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchan died, Qi took no food or drink for seven days, wept without cease morning and evening, and ate no salted food or vegetables with sauce.

sentences.zh: 每營買祭奠，身自看視，號泣不自持。

translations.literal: Whenever he arranged and purchased offerings he personally inspected them, wailing until he could not control himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he arranged offerings for sacrifice he inspected them himself, wailing until he could no longer hold himself together.

sentences.zh: 朔望節歲，絕而復續，吐血數升。

translations.literal: At the new and full moons and festival days he would faint and revive, vomiting several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: At the new and full moons and festival days he would faint and revive again, vomiting several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 時何胤、謝朏竝隱東山，遺書敦譬，誡以毀滅。

translations.literal: At the time He Yin and Xie Tiao were both in seclusion on Mount Dongshan; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him, warning against self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin and Xie Tiao were then in seclusion on Mount Dongshan; they sent letters earnestly urging him not to destroy himself through grief.

sentences.zh: 至祥禫，暮夢見其父，慟哭而絕。

translations.literal: At the auspicious and duchan rites, one evening he dreamed he saw his father, wailed in grief, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the auspicious and duchan mourning rites, one evening he dreamed of his father, wailed in grief, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，胤兄點見栖歎曰：「卿風韻如此，雖獲嘉譽，不永年矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yin's elder brother Dian, on seeing Qi, sighed and said, "With bearing such as yours, though you win fine praise, you will not live to old age."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yin's elder brother Dian saw Qi, he sighed and said, "With bearing such as yours, though you win fine praise, you will not live long."

sentences.zh: 」卒時年三十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 當世咸嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: All his contemporaries sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: All his contemporaries mourned him with regret.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，剡縣有小兒，年八歲，與母俱得赤班病。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, in Shan county there was a small boy of eight who, with his mother, contracted red-spotted disease.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, in Shan county there was a boy of eight who, with his mother, contracted red-spotted fever.

sentences.zh: 母死，家人以小兒猶惡，不令其知。

translations.literal: The mother died; the family, because the boy was still gravely ill, did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: The mother died; because the boy was still gravely ill, the family kept it from him.

sentences.zh: 小兒疑之，問云：「母嘗數問我病，昨來覺聲羸，今不復聞，何謂也？

translations.literal: The boy grew suspicious and asked, "Mother often asked after my illness; yesterday her voice sounded weak, and today I hear her no more—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The boy grew suspicious and asked, "Mother often asked after my illness; yesterday her voice sounded weak, and today I hear nothing—what has happened?"

sentences.zh: 」因自投下牀，匍匐至母尸側，頓絕而死。

translations.literal: He threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's corpse, and died in a sudden collapse.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's body, and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 鄉隣告之縣令宗善才，求表廬，事竟不行。

translations.literal: Neighbors reported it to the Magistrate Zong Shancai, who requested a memorial lodge; in the end the matter was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors reported it to Magistrate Zong Shancai, who asked that a memorial lodge be posted; in the end the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 陸絳字魏卿，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jiang, style name Weiqing, was a man of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiang, courtesy name Weiqing, was from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父閑，字遐業，有風概，與人交，不苟合。

translations.literal: His father Xian, style name Xiaye, had moral bearing; in dealings with others he would not join company casually.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian, courtesy name Xiaye, had strong moral bearing and would not join company with others lightly.

sentences.zh: 少為同郡張緒所知，仕至揚州別駕。

translations.literal: In youth he was recognized by Zhang Xu of the same commandery and rose to Vice Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was recognized by Zhang Xu of the same commandery and rose to Vice Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，閑謂所親曰：「宮車晏駕，百司將聽於冢宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Xian said to those close to him, "The imperial carriage has departed at dusk; the hundred offices will now heed the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Xian told those close to him, "The emperor is dead; the hundred offices will now take their orders from the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 主王地重才弱，必不能振，難將至矣。

translations.literal: Our lord the prince holds weighty territory but weak talent—he surely cannot rally support; trouble is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Our prince holds great territory but lacks strength—he cannot rally the realm, and trouble is coming.

sentences.zh: 」乃感心疾，不復預州事。

translations.literal: He then suffered heart ailment and no longer took part in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill at heart and withdrew from provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺史始安王遙光反，事敗，閑以綱佐被召至杜姥宅，尚書令徐孝嗣啟閑不預逆謀，未及報，徐世檦令殺之。

translations.literal: The Governor, Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, rebelled; when the affair failed, Xian as a senior aide was summoned to Lady Du's residence. The Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi memorialized that Xian had not joined the plot, but before a reply came Xu Shizhen ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an rebelled; when the plot failed, Xian as a senior aide was summoned to Lady Du's residence. Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi reported that Xian had not joined the conspiracy, but before a reply came Xu Shizhen ordered him killed.

sentences.zh: 絳時隨閑，抱閑頸乞代死，遂并見殺。

translations.literal: Jiang was then with Xian; he embraced Xian's neck and begged to die in his place, and both were killed together.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was with him; he threw his arms around Xian's neck and begged to die in his stead, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：澆風一起，人倫毀薄，抑引之教徒聞，珪璋之璞罕就。

translations.literal: The Historian says: When the thin current of custom rises, human relations are ruined and made shallow; the teaching of restraint and guidance is heard only in name, and the uncut jade of ritual and virtue is rarely perfected.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian says: When shallow custom takes hold, human bonds fray; the teaching of restraint is heard only in name, and the uncut jade of virtue is rarely perfected.

sentences.zh: 若令事長移忠，儻非行舉，薑桂辛酸，容遷本質。

translations.literal: If one were to let service to elders shift into loyalty to the state, perhaps without conduct worthy of recommendation, ginger and cassia in their bitterness might yet return to their native substance.
translations.idiomatic: If serving one's elders could truly ripen into loyalty to the state—if recommendation were not required—then even ginger and cassia in their bitterness might return to their true nature.

sentences.zh: 而旌閭變里，問餼存牢，不過鰥寡齊矜，力田等勸。

translations.literal: Yet posting gates and renaming lanes, sending inquiries and maintaining the granary, amounted to no more than equal pity for widowers and widows and encouragement for those who tilled with equal effort.
translations.idiomatic: Yet posting honor at gates and renaming lanes, sending inquiries and maintaining granaries, amounted to little more than pitying widows and orphans alike and encouraging diligent farmers.

sentences.zh: 其於扶獎名教，未為多也。

translations.literal: As for supporting and exalting the teaching of names and norms, this was not much.
translations.idiomatic: As for truly upholding the teaching of ritual and morality, it was not much.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝為行首，義實因心。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Filial piety is the head of conduct; righteousness truly springs from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Filial piety leads all conduct; righteousness springs from the heart.

sentences.zh: 白華秉節，寒木齊心。

translations.literal: White blossoms hold their nodes; cold trees share one heart.
translations.idiomatic: White blossoms hold their stems; cold trees share one heart.
